text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The Warsaw-based Bank Handlowy is entitled to demand an income tax deduction of 1.6 million zlotys in return for an unreturned credit granted to a state-owned paper mill which was guaranteed by the state treasury, Poland's Supreme Administrative Court said.

- Poland's industrial output capacity increased and the industrial climate improved in Octobber, but it was associated with falling orders and growing inventories, a report by the Warsaw School of Economics Economic Development Institute said.
- Poland's old age pensions will grow by 11.6 percent and salaries by 18.8 percent next year, the finance ministry said.
- Wavin Metalplast-Buk pipe and tile maker has invested two million zlotys in the plant's boiler modernisation in line with the environmental regulations to come into force as of January 1 next year.
- The United States Agency for International Development (USAID) has granted $6.5 million for professional training programmes to be conducted for Polish businessmen in the next three years.

- Netia Group, Poland's biggest private telecom operator will provide 111,000 new lines for subscribers in Silesia, southern Poland. The Netia South branch has received a $115 million credit to carry out the project.
- Akzo Nobel Dutch chemical concern will invest in Poland's paint and lacquer plants in Wloclawek and Gorzow, the concern's president Syb Bergsma said.
- The Wroclaw-based Pafawag rolling stock maker and the German ADTranz and Stadler AG have signed a contract on rail-bus production in the Wroclaw plant.
- Hypo-Bank Poland has increased its capital to 89.5 million zlotys from 34 million zlotys. The bank will soon open a new branch in Wroclaw, southwestern Poland.
NOWA EUROPA
- Poland's food prices in October 20-30 rose 0.3 percent against the same period in September, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- The listed Moststal Zabrze construction firm wants to build a 300 m mast for the Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA) state-owned telecom monopolist in Belchatow, southern Poland.
- By the end of the year Citroen Poland will sell 7,000 cars which gives it a 1.75 percent share in the market, the company president Alain Martinez said.
- The bankrupt Stocznia Gdanska shipyard will be able to operate until the end of 1997, the Gdansk provincial court said.
- The listed Beton Stal construction firm will carry out contracts worth $251,528 over an unspecified time, while its subsidiary Bestaco Ltd. will construct a building worth 2.762 million zlotys.

- The TU Compensa insurance firm, controlled by the listed Mostostal-Export construction firm, has reported a gross profit growth in the third quarter of 1996 tpo 2.2 million zlotys, 30 times more than in the same period last year.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- A court appointed management has taken over the Feniks insurance company as the result of the firm's financial troubles, Poland's State Insurance Supervision Office director Jan Grzelak said.
- The Lentex floor lining maker, controlled by the First National Investment Fund (NFI) has presented a share issue prospectus to the Polish securities commission.
ZYCIE WARSZAWY
- Poland's year-on-year inflation will reach 17.9 percent in December, Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko said.
- Era GSM digital mobile phone subscribers cannot use their phones in the city of Szczecin for technical reasons despite the operation's initiation by the company.
PARKIET
- The listed Elektrim electrical engineering firm will provide spare parts to the Electric Power Industry of Serbia worth $3.196 million.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
